chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah, Most High, support him—informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about the person in janabah: may he recite the Qur'an? He said: “There is nothing between him and seven verses.”

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: the Qur'an, the revealed Book of Allah
key_terms.سَبْعِ: seven, indicating the stated numerical limit

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah recite the Qur'an, and what is the limit?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on Qur'an recitation for a person in the state of janabah. It indicates a limit connected to seven verses, showing a legal boundary discussed in the jurisprudence of ritual purity and Qur'an recitation.
